reason: FastStone already does what I need every day and I have my muscle memory in it. The portable zip costs me nothing to try, but I don't see enough reason to swap a tool that works.
why_switch_or_not: I'd unzip the portable build and throw a few PSDs, AIs and alpha PNGs at it, mostly out of curiosity about the format coverage and the speed claims. But it lists a gallery, an editor, video, audio, 3D models and a scanner importer, which is the opposite of 'just a viewer that stays out of my way', and FastStone's full-screen mode, browser and simple editor are already in my hands daily. A one-person 0.4.1 with no plug-ins and English-only UI doesn't give me enough reason to move my file associations.
current_app_pros: FastStone's full-screen mode with the hover toolbars, the thumbnail browser and the quick editor all in one small tool I know by heart. It opens my everyday JPG/PNG/PSD fast enough and I don't have to think about it.
current_app_pains: Rapid next/back through big folders lags a bit and it won't open some of the stranger formats (AI/PSD fidelity is not perfect, alpha handling is so-so). Nothing that makes me want to switch.
objection: Another image viewer? Mine already works fine, and this one is a one-developer 0.4.1 that tries to be a gallery, editor, media player and 3D viewer, when all I want is a viewer.
would_change_my_mind: If PSD and AI files with transparency showed exactly like in Photoshop/Illustrator, with colour-managed accuracy I can verify on my own files, and a pure viewing mode that hides the editor, gallery and everything else.
